utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. As you can see, unfortunately Judge Van den Wyngaert will not be able to sit today. We anticipate she will be able to join us tomorrow. If I could remind you of the affirmation which is still applicable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we could please go back to MFI P00369. And just to remind you, Mr. Kuehnel, we left off on Friday when we were dealing with the telephone records and that is at tab 34 in the hard copy binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I could please ask Madam Registrar to turn to page 11 in that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuehnel, if you can draw your attention to the 14th column from the top, the number that you believe was used by Johan Tarculovski, called Aleksander Janevski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you know who this is, Aleksander Janevski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's the brother of Vlado Janev.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what is the basis of your belief that the person listed on this call, Aleksander Janevski, is the same person who is the brother of Vlado Janev?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlado Janev, in his interview, he accepted this being his brother's name, Aleksander Janevski. The address given next to the name Aleksander Janevski is identical with the address of the brother of Vlado Janev. It's the house next to it. And looking at the criminal records, you can also see the relationship between the two. You can deduct it. Apart from that, the telephone number was also given in conjunction with an RFA request to our office, directed to our office.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that is the same telephone number that is --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same telephone that's given here. Apart from that, the statements given by third persons also said that they were brothers. And the two names, Vlado Janev and Aleksander Janevski, also appear in the list of the 25th and 26th of July, 2001, and both persons were also given by third persons relating to the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you refer to the list of 25th/26th July, 2001, just for the record you're referring to P00436, the list of -- indicating persons who received weapons on that day from PSOLO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you have occasion, Mr. Kuehnel, to attend at that address that is listed as boulevard Ilinden 108 that you associated with Aleksander Janevski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Ms. Issa. I went there with my colleague from OTP, Mr. Jozefciak, and we tried to -- to give -- to submit a summons to both brothers there. When we went there, both brothers were not present, but I talked to a woman who introduced herself as being the wife of Aleksander Janevski. And in a statement that she made, it was a proactive statement, this woman, who was emotionally upset at this moment in time, she said that her husband was in Ljuboten and he was also wounded there, the person who is supposed to live at boulevard Ilinden 108.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can then please ask Madam Registrar to turn to page 9 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to about the 10th or 11th column from the top on page 9. You see there are a series of calls from the number that you believe was being used by Johan Tarculovski to a Zoran Jovanovski on the 12th of August, 2001. And that number is listed as 70225660. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that, Ms. Issa. It's Zoran Jovanovski. The address is Klenoec 29-A and the name and this address is also given in the replies of the Ministry of the Interior to an RFA. In this RFA, Zoran Jovanovski was also being given as the owner of the security firm Kometa, and there are -- is a number of other documents where you can identify this link, also in some criminal files and also in statements given by third persons through the OTP. The same applies to this person, that this name is given on the list of the 26th and -- 25th and 26th July, 2001. Mr. Zoran Jovanovski was also being named as an -- an accused, or as a suspect, rather. I'm correcting myself. He has also accepted that he is the owner of the company named Kometa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can stop you there for a moment, Mr. Kuehnel, when you say this person was named as a suspect are you referring to a suspect interview that the Office of the Prosecutor carried out with Mr. Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And have you had occasion from all the information that you've received to compare the telephone number that we see on the telephone log with the information that you received through the RFAs?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The number is identical. And this was the number given in conjunction with Mr. Zoran Jovanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to page 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the 10th column from the bottom, we see here the number that you believe was used by Johan Tarculovski calling an individual called Goce Ralevski on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please turn back to page 11. If I can draw your attention to the 15th column from the top we see here that the number that you believe was being used by Johan Tarculovski calling Goce Ralevski on 12 August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to save time, Your Honours, Mr. Kuehnel has already testified on page -- transcript page 7962 that this name is referenced on exhibit number P00436, the list from 25/26 July. And finally, in respect of this document, if we can please go to page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the name Mario Jurisic who is -- which is at the 10th column from the top. The number you believe was being used by Johan Tarculovski called Mario Jurisic on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we could please turn to page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the third column from the bottom. We see a name there, Nikolce Grozdanovski and it appears that the number you believe is being used by Johan Tarculovski was calling that number on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Kuehnel, who is Nikolce Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikolce Grozdanovski is a member of the army. He is a commander of the 100-millimetre battery [as interpreted] of the 3rd Battalion -- of the -- Motor Brigade and because of this Mr. Grozdanovski was also interviewed by us. And he was also present also when the events at Ljuboten happened. He was in his post.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to page 57 in that document. Actually, if question first -- Madam Registrar, if we can please first go to page 54.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, if you look on your screen, that's the commencement of the log of the -- relating to the incoming logs -- incoming calls, rather, of that same number you believe to be used by Johan Tarculovski. If we can then please go to page 57. If I can draw your attention to the third and fourth and fifth column from the top. You see the same numbers that we've seen earlier are calling the number you believe to be Johan Tarculovski's number, listed as Zoran Jovanovski and Ljube Krstevski, on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can look at the 11th column from the bottom, Once again, you see Ljube Krstevski and the individual we just spoke about a moment ago, Grozdanovski, Nikolce, also calling the number you believe to be Johan Tarculovski's number on 12 August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: At this stage, Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I object to having this document received in evidence, since it was not ascertained that the telephone number belongs to Johan Tarculovski. On the contrary, from the evidence of this witness, it was established that this phone number was used by the person named Gjorgi Todorovski as it is stated in the document N000-7356, N000-757 -- 7357 and this witness only makes a conjecture that the person Johan Tarculovski has used this phone number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This witness has already testified that he received information from Ljube Krstevski that this number was being used by Johan Tarculovski. We also saw evidence that this number frequently called and was being called by a person identified as Mr. Tarculovski's wife during that same period of time, and we saw evidence that the diary of M-084 refers to the name Johan with that number written down next to it. And therefore, in my submission, taking into account all of those factors, I would submit there is sufficient evidence that this number was being used by Johan Tarculovski and it's -- it is certainly something that goes to the weight of the evidence as to -- as opposed to its admission. I would submit that at this stage it would be admissible on this basis and it would be a question of fact for the Chamber to determine whether or not in fact this was a number that was being used by Johan Tarculovski during that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received as an exhibit. It is not tendered on the basis that it is shown to be the telephone owned by but that there is evidence capable of establishing, if it is accepted by the Chamber, that it was a telephone used by the accused Johan Tarculovski and will be received on that basis.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will retain the same number but will become Exhibit P369, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to tab 42, 65 ter number 1007.1. If we can slightly enlarge the first page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see on your screen, Mr. Kuehnel, there's a number listed there as an outgoing number, 70243818. Do you recognise that number?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who does it belong to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official number of the Ministry of Interior and it belongs to Ljube Krstevski in his function as -- in 2001, he was the OVA commander for Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what is the basis of your belief?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically there are two reasons. First of all --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can actually stop you there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can please go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to that first page, towards the end of the page there appears to be a telephone call made by Radojko Lozanovski to Ljube Krstevski's number on 11 August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you look at about the fourth column from the bottom, there appears to be a telephone call made by what you believe to be Ljube Krstevski's number to the same number that you believe to be Johan Tarculovski's number, 279417, do you see, on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you compare that -- this log-book with the incoming calls of the previous log-book for that number, 279417, during the same time-period?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, as a kind of blind test to determine whether, with the log-books or this evidence, the criteria were in harmony, that is, the outgoing an incoming numbers showed the same time and date stamps with the relevant numbers, a quality check, to see whether we could find the same information on both lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did they match?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please turn to page 2 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd just like to draw your attention to the second column from the top, we that number that you indicated was belonging to Ljube Krstevski calling Zoran Jovanovski and then below that the same number calling Ilija Sovkovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Madam Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And both those calls were made on the 12th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we didn't realise that it was an attempt to tender the document at this stage. We have no objection to the document. We would simply wish to indicate that for this document and the next one that two of the individuals mentioned on this list M-053 and M-084 have been -- have appeared as witnesses in this case and were not asked questions in relation to this document. It's therefore our understanding that the document is tendered for the purpose indicated by my colleague, namely, the fact that certain phone calls were directed to certain persons but not in relation to the content of any such calls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My observation was misleading, and I'm sorry I did mislead you. We're receiving at the moment the oral evidence allowing it to continue. It's not yet been tendered. I should have been more careful in my language. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, in line 11, 1, examination, and not cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you can please then look towards the bottom of that page, Mr. Kuehnel. It's about seven or eight columns from the bottom, and we see that number that you've identified as belonging to Ljube Krstevski calling Radojko Lozanovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Madam Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And right below that we see the same number calling the number 279417, which is listed MOI of the RM that you have previously identified as the number you believed to be used by Johan Tarculovski on the 12th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now did you compare that number 279417 with the incoming calls for 279417 that you believed belonged to Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did they match?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has indicated its position sufficiently to accept this on the basis that has been indicated already by Ms. Issa. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P535, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to tab 43, 65 ter number 1007.2. If I can ask Madam Registrar to please enlarge the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, at the very top, Mr. Kuehnel, you see this is marked as income calls for that number 70243818, the number you identified as belonging to Ljube Krstevski, and we see that at page 1, the number 279417, which is about at the middle of the page, was calling the number you identified as belonging to Ljube Krstevski. And that is at column number 87 or at least there's a -- by way of reference we can look at the duration, time of the telephone call at the very last column to the right, it says 87 and below that 25. Those are the telephone calls that I'm referring to, Mr. Kuehnel. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if I can draw your attention to a couple of columns below that, the duration time being used as a reference point once again as number 43 and we see, once again, Ljube Krstevski's number calling 70279417 on the 10th of August at about 7.12 in the evening. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And finally, if you look at the very bottom of that page, the last two telephone calls, Ljube Krstevski's number is, once again, calling the number 279417 on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, did you compare the incoming calls from that number, 243818 in this log-book with the outgoing calls of that same number that we saw in the log-book marked as P30069, which is the outgoing calls of 279417 that you believe was being used by Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did they match?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: At this stage I'd like to tender this exhibit, this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P536, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, did you at some stage attend the intelligence services of the Macedonian Ministry of Interior or what is none as the UBK/DBK in February 2007?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Ms. Issa, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you were there did you request any information or documents relating to radio communications that related to the events in Ljuboten in 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did ask for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you provided with any such documents or information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I received a negative response. I received nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you advised whether or not any such intercepts or documents existed or were available at the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was told that the service had no such recordings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to 65 ter number 246 at tab 47 in the binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now we see a document on the screen, Mr. Kuehnel, that is titled: Persons responsible at check-points in the area of Ljubanci and Ljuboten villages in August 2001. And it appears to be stamped and signed by the commander of the police station Mirkovci. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, I know this document. I received this as a response to a RFA from the government of Macedonia, through the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P537, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to 65 ter number 477, at tab 48 in the binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We see that this is a document from the Ministry of Interior dated 12 August 2001 and at the very top is -- says check-point Ljubanci. And it's titled: An order for performing service. And at the very bottom it is signed by commander Lieutenant Slavko Ivanovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know this document. This is a document that we also received in response to a RFA.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P538, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to 65 ter number 1031, tab 49.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is a document, once again, from the Ministry of Interior, the Republic of Macedonia, dated August 12, 2001. And, again, it is titled: Order to carry out a task and specifically refers to the concrete task as being between 08 and 20 hours to provide complete security at the facility by undertaking measures of monitoring and observing with the aim of preventing attacks, carrying out or causing diversion terrorist actions over the facility and in relation to OA Ramno. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document is one that I know. It came from OVR Cair, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P539, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to 65 ter 1030, at tab 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This document is titled: Report. And it refers to, "During our working hours between 0800 and 2000 hours we acted according to order number 2396," which references the previous document that we just saw, that same number for the order. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know this document. It is only page 2 of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can please ask that this be admitted into evidence at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P540, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please go to tab 51, 65 ter 1037.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, this document is also from the Ministry of Interior dated 14 August 2001 and it's in regards to a Hermelin vehicle as noted at the top right-hand corner and it's referred to -- it is in fact an order for performing duty number 2589, signed by the commander, Lieutenant Ivanovski, Slavko, the length of duty, as noted two lines from the bottom, is from 7.00 a.m. on the 14th of August, 2001, to 7.00 p.m. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do that, Madam Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this document. It is in response to a RFA and I received this personally from the OVR Cair. Originally it comes from the police station in Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P541, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters need to note that there is a very high level of background noise in the courtroom and it interferes with our work, so please use keyboards sparingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Kuehnel, at any time during your involvement in this case from November 2001 to May 2002, did the Macedonian authorities ever ask the Office of the Prosecutor to provided them with the results of interviews of witnesses? And just to correct myself, I know you were involved from the beginning of October -- or from around October 2003, but at any time during the course of your involvement in this case, did the Macedonian authorities, from the November 2001 to May 2002 ever request the results of interviews of witnesses from the OTP, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you said, I started in October 2003 to work in this field, and after this period I know nothing about this matter. The only thing that came to my knowledge, and this is something I derived from the court files, was a letter to the OTP in which I believe Prosecutor Dzikov presented the results of the ballistic or requested the results of the ballistic examination, and what came of that, but I was told that both of these documents would be found in the court files.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But apart from the request for the ballistic examinations, were you aware, just to clarify, of any other request made by the Macedonian authorities to the OTP, particularly in respect of information or interviews regarding witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kuehnel. My name is Guenael Mettraux and together with Ms. Edina Residovic I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you agree that an important aspect of your work as an investigator to ensure the safekeeping of the material and information which you collect as part of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that the care that must be paid in that regard would apply to all types of information obtained, whether they are statements, records of interviews or documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the purpose of so doing is, I suggest to you, to ensure the integrity of the material in question, and also to try to keep as complete and as accurate a record of your investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I suppose that it so happens, as in any other institution, that material or information that has been collected sometimes get lost in the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, obviously it can happen. It shouldn't happen, but wherever humans are at work, mistakes are being made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where such mistake occur, this would mean in practice that the record -- if a document has been lost or some information has been lost, the record of the information which you receive would be incomplete. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a document has been lost, then of course you have also lost information up to some extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that one record or one particular record that was lost by you is the record of an interview which you had conducted with a person by the name of Boban Utkovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite, Mr. Mettraux. I conducted the interview. I wrote down the contents of the interview. I took the record home and put it on the OTP drive. Unfortunately, however, and without any bad will on anyone's part, this document was lost. My name -- it bears my name, I have written this document, but I cannot say that it was me who lost the document. But, of course, it's very annoying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kuehnel, we'd like to make it clear to you that I'm not suggesting in any way that there was any bad will in the loss of that document. But simply for the Judges to understand who we are talking about, is that correct that in August of 2001 Mr. Boban Utkovski was a member of the security arrangements or a body-guard of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that. But I'm not sure about his -- the way he spent his time. At a different moment of time of that year, he was also the deputy commander of the Lions formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you are aware, aren't you, that in August of 2001 Mr. Utkovski was still a member or a body-guard of the president of the republic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, he was a member of the Ministry of the Interior and he had the function of a body-guard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he was a body-guard to the president of the Republic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure about that. It could also be that he had this function for the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D1138.1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, are you familiar with this document which was obtained pursuant to a request for assistance by your office. Do you know this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a response to RFA 92 or 93. I already talked about that. That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry to please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, if you could locate the sixth name on that list in the fourth column from the left. Can you see the name of Utkovski Boban?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Mettraux, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the second column from the left which is the column relating to position in 2001, can you see it says: Independent inspector for presidential security in the presidential security unit. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got a problem with the transcript. Yes. Now, it's okay. Yes, of course I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you can see that it mentions the fact that Mr. Utkovski was a member of the presidential security in the presidential security unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. The document can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Kuehnel, that for several months this year, the Prosecution -- or well, in response Defence request the Prosecution had indicated that it had no record of an interview with Mr. Utkovski. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that after several month when the Prosecution indicated that it had no such record, finally a -- an investigator's note was produced. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the investigator's notes was produced by you, I believe, in late September based on the memory which you had of the interview with Mr. Utkovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in that note you indicated, among other things, that you had in fact met with Mr. Utkovski in November of 2004 in prison in Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in that same note you recorded the fact that Mr. Utkovski had indicated to you that he had not been in Ljuboten during the weekend of 10 and 12 of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there is a short statement that you made in this note to yourself or to the person to whom you directed the note and I would like to read it to you. You said this: "The subject could not be clear if or if not Mr. Utkovski was in possession of the phone number or only used the telephone number allegedly being in contact with Tarculovski." Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that a few day after you had prepared your first investigator note in relation to your meeting with Mr. Utkovski, the Defence asked you, through Mr. Saxon, to flesh out that note and in particular to indicate whether any document had been shown during your meeting with Mr. Utkovski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in response you said the following, I will read out to from the note, Mr. Kuehnel, and if you wish to see it, by all means say so. You said this: "It is very likely that I would have discussed some documents with Mr. Utkovski. It is possible that I discussed the fact that Mr. Utkovski's name appeared on a telephone records containing incoming and outgoing telephone calls on Johan Tarculovski's regular telephone during 10 to 12 August, 2001." Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, when you referred to certain telephone records and, quote/unquote, Mr. Tarculovski's regular phone, you were referring to the document which was shown to you some time ago by my colleague, Exhibit P2 -- P369. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite. I would agree that I possibly talked to him about this. I might have, but I can't quite recall whether I submitted this list to him or not, but I don't think so. But I don't want to speculate. And I also would like to state that it is exceptionally difficult in such a case, because just prior to that interview I conducted an interview with Goran Stojkov, and in his position, function, and also in his present situation, at that moment in time, was also in prison in Sutka.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may stop you here for a moment, let's stay with Mr. Utkovski here and we may come back to Mr. Stojkov a bit later, but I understand from your statement that you indicated in your note that you weren't sure whether or not you in fact showed the list to Mr. Utkovski, but my question was the list or the phone records to which you referred in your note and which you say you were not sure whether you showed him or not were the same phone records that were showed by my colleague to you a moment ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to conclude my reply. I was interrupted. My previous reply specifically was referring to the situation with Mr. Utkovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I started to explain why it was so difficult to recall this particular situation. The conversation that I had with Mr. Stojkov was almost identical in -- as far as the subjects were concerned, the things we talked about. Both persons were commanders of the Lions, both were in prison at that time. And I -- the reasons for talking to these two persons were identical, too. Now, for one, for Mr. Stojkov Goran we have got the investigator's notes. As far as Mr. Utkovski is concerned, we don't have them. Now, as to what I have shown to whom in that case, I really cannot recall that. Hence, it is very difficult for me to give a precise answer to your questions, Mr. Mettraux. From what I can recall generally speaking, I certainly had the list on me that you mentioned previously, but I cannot really recall whether I showed it to Mr. Utkovski or not. And this is my reply to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful, Mr. Kuehnel. Is it correct that another thing which you put in your investigator's notes which you produced recently is the fact that Mr. Utkovski indicated to you that the Lions had in fact not been in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite sure about that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I have a few general questions. Do you know a person by the name of Zlatko Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this person, but I've never met that person. And I know that we've got a witness statement of this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the assistance of the Chamber, Mr. Kuehnel, is it correct that in 2001 or in any case in August of 2001 Mr. Keskovski was the chief of the security of the president of the Republic, Mr. Trajkovski. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that in his statement to the Office of the Prosecutor Mr. -- which you have just indicated you knew about, Mr. Keskovski indicated that the president would sometime use the phone of his body-guards to get in touch with various people. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct also that Mr. Keskovski indicated to you that the president did so, that is, using the phone, in particular the phone of Mr. Keskovski to contact a number of people during the weekend 10-12 August 2001. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is correct, expressis verbis, literally yes, but all in all, yes, but I think one would need to read up on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall for instance that Mr. Keskovski indicated to your office that the president asked him to call General Metodija Stamboliski, then the Chief of Staff of the army, do you recall that, and that Mr. Keskovski did so?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. Generally speaking, but I cannot remember exactly what it says in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will in fairness assist you, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D526.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, this will be the OTP statement of Mr. Zlatko Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, but before we continue, I hate to interrupt the flow of my friend, but I do want to note for the record that this is a statement that actually was referred to at some point earlier during the trial. He was a witness that was removed from the Prosecution witness list at some stage during the course of this trial, and I don't want to interrupt the flow of my friend's cross-examination, but I just want to highlight the fact that, in my submission, we -- my friend needs to be cautious because I'm concerned that evidence is coming in through the back door that otherwise wouldn't have come in if -- given that this witness was not -- is not being called by the Prosecution. So I don't know if my friend is going to through the entirety of the statement or what the purpose is but I'm just rising at this stage to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's an interesting submission, Ms. Issa, and one that doesn't perhaps sit readily in the mouth of the Prosecution at the present time. It is almost an echo of submissions that were put against the way the Prosecution was leading certain evidence and which the Chamber has not been minded to act on and the Prosecution was allowed to proceed. And the same course will be followed for the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I can ask the assistance of the registry, and if we could turn to page 9 of the statement which is 1D00-4780, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I'll ask you to focus and with the assistance of the registry on paragraph 38 of the statement of Mr. Keskovski. And I will read out to you the first two sentence of that paragraph. It says this: "The president asked me to call General Metodija Stamboliski and ask him why the army helicopters were not supporting these people. First I spoke to the general and then the president and then again I spoke to the general about the situation in the area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you can see in the second sentence he recalls a second call to the General. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does that help you refresh your memory about this, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall also that Mr. Keskovski indicated to the Office of the Prosecutor that he called Mr. Tarculovski on behalf of the president. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that during this conversation the president then spoke on the phone of Mr. Keskovski to Major Despodov. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That must say that in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you, Mr. Kuehnel, to focus on the second paragraph on that page. That's paragraph 42 and a sentence starting with the word: "When I spoke with Johan Tarculovski." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it states the follows: "When I spoke with Johan Tarculovski I used my duty mobile phone. It might be one of the following two numbers: 070360000, or 070344044." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he also said the follow to go your colleague. He said this: "I do not know the number of the president mobile phone because we were changing it very frequently, for instance, I took the phone from the driver and I gave it to the president and vice versa. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you confirm perhaps for the record that, if you know, that at the time the driver of the president of the Republic of Macedonia in August of 2001 was a man by the man of Aco Mladenov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. But I can't recall that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should show you what is Rule 65 ter 1D1138.1 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry, please, to turn to page 1D00-9248 of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Mettraux please pause before asking the question because he is overlapping with the interpretation of the witness's words.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, are you able to see on the second range of columns the name Aco Mladenov. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you see that in the second column of that page which concerns the position in 2001, Mr. Mladenov is recorded as being independent inspector for escort security in the presidential security unit. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please now turn to what is now Exhibit P369, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, this will be, again, the list of the records of telephone numbers which you believe to be the telephone used by Mr. Tarculovski during the weekend 10 and 12 -- 10 to 12 of August of 2001 and beyond, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please first turn to page ET-N000-7433-055, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recognize this is the second part of that document, Mr. Kuehnel, simply to confirm that we are going into the part of the incoming calls, that is, the calls that came to the phone which you believe to be that of Mr. Tarculovski during that weekend. And if the registry could turn to page ET-N000-7433-058, please. Mr. Kuehnel, do you agree that we are on the list of incoming calls for the day the 11th of August of 2001, at least as the first part of that page is concerned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to you locate the telephone number four successive calls with the same number. It's 16, 17, 18 and 19th line. The number is 070344044. Can you locate these numbers?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this is one of the two numbers which Mr. Keskovski mentioned as his own in his statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And these calls were made on the 11th of August between 4.32 and 5.46 on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that these phone records are in fact consistent with the evidence or the information which Mr. Keskovski gave to you as far as the suggestion that he called Mr. Tarculovski on behalf of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this extent as to which he has stated it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We resume just after 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If the registry could stay in the same document but please turn to page ET-N000-733-009.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, we still on the same document but this time we're going to be in the outgoing calls from that number. And I'll ask to you locate a -- two particular calls which were made at 4.31 and 7.08 on the 11th of August of 2001, and they are number 13 and 14th on that list. Can you locate those telephone calls?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the bottom or the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: From the top, please. The telephone which is being called is 070344044 and they are two calls at 4.31 and 7.08. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that, again, you recall, is the number given by Mr. Keskovski as his telephone number. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that as far as those records are concerned, there appears to have been six calls between this particular telephone and the telephone of Mr. Keskovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the relationship between the names and the numbers and take that as read, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when I said six call, that would be between the 11th and the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could turn to page ET-N000-7433-011, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, we are still on the same document, still outgoing calls, but this time for the 12th of August of 2001. And I'd ask you to look at the list of phone calls which starts on the 13th line and go down to the 18th line. They are eight separate calls to the same number, Mr. Keskovski's number. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. And you would agree that these seven calls were made to the telephone number given by Mr. Keskovski as his own. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on his statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the calls in question were made on the 12th of August, between 10.16 and 8.30. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you have to say that you can't really tell whether it is a.m. or p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But would you agree that they appear to be listed in chronological order and that they simply used a 12-hour clock rather than a 24-hour clock. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I noticed that, but that's a conclusion. It's not actual knowledge. At least as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could turn, once again, to the incoming calls on that particular telephone number, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would ask the registry to go to page ET-N000-7433-059, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but could I please have the e-court page numbers for that so that I could follow along.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe this is the e-court number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, I was referring to page numbers before but that's is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can assist, this would be page 4 of the incoming calls, Your Honour. The incoming part has been re-numbered. It doesn't follow the numbering of the outgoing calls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Kuehnel. If could you look at this page and the fifth, sixth and seventh lines of that document. Can you see again the number given by Mr. Keskovski as his telephone number, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And from this document it would appear that the calls, the incoming calls were made at 11.39, 5.38 and 10.08 on the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would it be correct, then, to say that on the -- for the period 11 to 12th of August of 2001, the phone of Mr. Keskovski and this particular phone were in contacts approximately or at least nine -- on nine separate occasions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as nine connections are concerned, I agree. Whether this had to do with the subscriber Keskovski or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall that in the note that you prepared a few weeks ago you recorded the following, and I will read out to you. If I wish to see the note, Mr. Kuehnel, please ask and I will show it to you. But you said this: "The subject could not be cleared if or if not Mr. Utkovski was in possession of the phone number or only used the telephone number allegedly being in contact with Tarculovski." Do you recall putting that down in your note?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the subsequent note that you prepared again of a few days later in early October of this year you said, and I quote: "It is possible that you," Mr. Kuehnel, "discussed the fact that Mr. Utkovski's name appeared on telephone records containing incoming and outgoing telephones on Johan Tarculovski's cellular phone during 10, 12 August." Do you recall putting that down in your note?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall also, Mr. Kuehnel, that during your interview with Mr. Utkovski in November of 2004, Mr. Utkovski had indicated to you that the president of the Republic, Mr. Trajkovski, had been using his phone during the weekend 10 to 12 of August, 2001? Do you recall him telling you that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, I can't recall this in such detail for the reasons I've stated before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D526, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, this will be, again, the statement, the OTP statement, of Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to go to page 10 of the statement which is page 1D00-4781 in e-court. Thank you. And if the registry could focus on paragraph 43 of this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I'd like to read out a passage of the interview or the statement, rather, that was taken of Mr. Keskovski by your colleague at paragraph 43. The follow is being recorded: "Being asked if it is possible that the president was using the phone of Boban Utkovski, I say that it was possible but only in limited occasions, since Utkovski had a permanent mobile phone number. It could have happened if the president needed it and asked Utkovski to use his phone, but I'm sure that the president did not use Utkovski mobile phone for more than one day." Is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that this particular line of questions asked of Mr. Keskovski was the result of what Mr. Utkovski had told you a few month earlier, namely, that the president had used his phone during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really think so. As I said before, I can't really remember this passage in the statement. Certainly there were several reasons. I didn't conduct the interview; it is not my own. Of course the subscriber information led certainly to the fact that this was mentioned, but I'm sure you will know that a telephone list in the reply of RFA 92 was also listed giving information that there was certainly justified doubts as to Mr. Utkovski used this special number or not. But I'm sure we will have time to talk about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to go back for a moment, Mr. Kuehnel, to the telephone list again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P369, please. Exhibit P369.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we'll start perhaps with the incoming calls on that particular telephone number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to go to page ET-N000-7433-057, which would be page 2 in the paper version.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, as indicated, this is -- or you will agree that this is a list of incoming calls which cover, for the first part of the page, the 10th of August of 2001, and at the bottom of the page, starts with the 11th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to locate on this list of incoming calls those which are listed in the 8th -- I believe 7, 8, 9 and 10th line of that document. Can you see those? I'm sorry, 8, 9, 10, and 11.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The three that are marked as Utkovski [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuehnel. Perhaps we have a little dispute on the number. I would --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Kuehnel. You will agree that between 10.15 and 6.45 on the 10th of August 2001 there were four phone calls coming to that phone from the phone of Mr. Boban Utkovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the subscriber information for Utkovski and assume that this was his number, then your argument certainly holds water. But there are other possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you agree that this is a list that records the incoming telephone calls on that particular number for the period 11 August 2001 and then it starts with the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to you locate the 12th call on that page and ask you to locate the name of Mr. Boban Utkovski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But I would like to ask you perhaps to give me that in paper form. It is perhaps simpler for me if you could give me this in a binder if it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kuehnel, I would be delighted to do so. I have only one copy and I would ask perhaps if my colleague has an extra copy. I believe it is in your binder --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, okay. If I could take this copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be tab 34 in your binder, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know if I can find it.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would be page 3 of the incoming calls.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the outgoing calls here. Are you sure that it was 34?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps if it assists, it's at tab 34 at the very end of the page, after the green marker, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I only have the Macedonian version. Okay. Let's continue. Let's forget that, I'm sorry, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Kuehnel, and we'll see whether we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, if your binder is the same as mine, you have at tab 34, before the green binder, the English form, and it commences with outgoing calls.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I flicked over one page too many. I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for Your Honour's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, if I could ask to you turn to page 3 of the incoming calls, please.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask you to locate the -- what I believe to the 12th recorded call on that page. It's incoming call from the telephone number of Mr. Boban Utkovski at 12.38. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this is a call that is recorded as having been made at 12.38 on the 11th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look further down the page towards the end, there is another number at 12.11, which is recorded as having come from the telephone number of Mr. Boban Utkovski at 12.11 on the 12th of August, 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can now turn to the outgoing calls from that particular telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry to turn to page ET-N000-7433-005.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Kuehnel, this would be page 4 on the paper version. Do you agree, Mr. Kuehnel, that this particular page relates to outgoing calls made from that particular phone on the 10th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see six of these connection dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that according to this record, six calls were made to Mr. Boban Utkovski or the phone recorded as the phone of Mr. Boban Utkovski on the 10th of August of 2001, between 10.20 and 3.09 on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My normal parlance, I would say that the links between these two numbers was certainly established. Whether Boban Utkovski in fact was in possession of this telephone or not, I cannot say and I cannot tell from this. As I said before, these are connection data and not conversation data.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for this specification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to page 8 in the paper version, and ET-N000-7433-009 [sic], please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree first perhaps that this is the record of outgoing telephone conversation for the 11th of August of 2001 and then it starts with a few records from the 12th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you in the records for the 11th of August of 2001 to locate what I believe to be the sixth such call, can you see that there's the record of an outgoing call from this particular telephone number to the telephone number recorded as that of Mr. Boban Utkovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that particular call is recorded as having taken place at 11.50 on the 11th of August, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please turn to the next page. It's page 9 in the paper version. Do you agree, Mr. Kuehnel, that this is the record of this particular telephone for the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said number nine, didn't you? If I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's for the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to go up from the bottom of the page, do you agree that on the 12th of August of 2001 at 7.53, there is the record of a call from that particular number to the telephone number of Mr. Boban Utkovski. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that for the period 10 to 12 of August of 2001, this particular telephone number was in contact approximately 14 times, six incoming and eight outgoing, with the telephone number of the body-guard of the president, Mr. Utkovski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. I haven't really counted, by I'm sure I trust your mathematical skills.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Do you recall I've asked you whether you remembered Mr. Aco Mladenov being the driver of the president at the time, a moment ago. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we talked about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we've established, I believe, that Mr. Mladenov was a member of the security of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the data in the appendix of the RFA 92, one can conclude so. Yes, one could say that, one could conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know a person by the name of Vladimir Dimovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown again Rule 65 ter 1D1138.1, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, if you can look again, this is the same document, the one that you have just referred to in relation to Mr. Mladenov. And I'll ask the registry to please turn to page 3 of that document, which would be 1D00-9246. Can you locate, Mr. Kuehnel, the second name on that list, the name of Mr. Vladimir Dimovski, can you see that name?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That's the same name as that written in the same way in the telephone evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that in the column, the second column that relates to the position of that person in 2001 is recorded as an escort inspector for presidential security in the presidential security unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so I can see from what is in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we go back please to Exhibit P369.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: First perhaps I'll ask you a general question, Mr. Kuehnel. When you reviewed these telephone records which we have been discussing now for a while, did you become aware of frequent contacts between this particular telephone, the records of which you had and the telephone numbers of Aco Mladenov and Vladimir Dimovski, who were member of the security of the president at the time?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is obvious. And these names are -- match the appendix to the RFA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please turn to page 5 in the paper version which is ET-N000-7433-006.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, that's page 5 of the paper version, outgoing calls. Do you agree first that this particular page records the outgoing calls from this particular phone for the period of 10 August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And towards the upper part of this page, can you identify, I believe, nine outgoing calls from this telephone to the telephone of the body-guard of the president, Mr. Vladimir Dimovski. Can you see those?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can see that. It's the same, as I said before. It says that there is a connection between the two numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those connections -- I apologise to the interpreters. And those connections took place on the 10th of August of 2001 between 1.11 and the last calls appear to be at 3.13. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to you go further down in the document. Is it correct that the next person whose name is recorded as having been called by that particular number is Mr. Aco Mladenov, the driver of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct on that on day, the 10 August of 2001, Mr. Mladenov was called by that particular number 14 times, 1-4, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, those calls took place between 1.08 and 11.01. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can turn now to page ET-N000-7433-009, Mr. Kuehnel, that would be page 8 in the paper version. And I'd ask to you to locate three successive calls, I believe they're the 11th, 12th and 13th calls recorded on that page and they are outgoing calls. Can you see those? They are recorded as having been made to the phone number of Aco Mladenov. Can you see them?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said three.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those calls are recorded as having been made on the 11th of August of 2001 between 2.57 and 9.54. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the next page, please, page 9 in the paper version.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to ask to you turn to the last-but-one call recorded on that page, which is recorded as having been made to the phone number of Vladimir Dimovski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. 9.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be 9.35 on the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. Is it correct that at 8.46, still on the 12th of August of 2001, there is another call recorded as coming from this particular phone and going again to the telephone of Mr. Mladenov on the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct? That's the third line.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can now turn to the incoming calls, please, on that particular phone. This would be ET-N000-7433-057, which would be page 2 on the paper version of incoming calls. This is a page that we've already seen in relation to Mr. Boban Utkovski, but I will ask you to go further down. First perhaps to ask you that do you agree that this relates to incoming calls for the 10th of August of 2001 and then there's a number of phones for the next day, the 11th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be page 2 of the incoming calls.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, that's right. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that at 3.07 on the 10th of August 2001 there's a particular phone call, an incoming call that is recorded from the telephone of Mr. Dimovski Vladimir, a body-guard of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just underneath that particular call there are nine telephone calls recorded, again on the 10th of August of 2001, between this particular phone and the phone of Mr. Mladenov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those phone calls simply for the record were made between 11.02 and 11.31 on the 10th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
