utterances.text: First, if we can look at the records, Mr. Kuehnel, of phone records for the 11th of August of 2001, I'd like you to locate one particular call that took place at 10.26 and which is said to have come from the phone of Mr. Mladenov Aco. Can you locate this one?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look further down on the page it's I think the fifth line from the bottom, do you agree that there's another call, incoming call that is recorded from Mr. Mladenov, this time at 11.46 on the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps, if you can trust my mathematics again, would you agree that those records suggest that between the period 10 to 12th of August of 2001 there were approximately 40, 4-0, phone conversation or phone calls in any case between the phone of Mr. Mladenov and Mr. Dimovski, on the one hand, and the phone that you say was used by Mr. Tarculovski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do beg your pardon. As far as the connection data is concerned as to how use the telephone [as interpreted], and somebody else maybe as Mr. Tarculovski, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful for that specification, Mr. Kuehnel. And would you agree that this suggests that as far as those records are concerned, in any case, there would have been approximately, I believe, 64 or 65 contact calls between this particular phone and members of the security of the president: Mr. Utkovski, Mr. Mladenov, and Mr. Dimovski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you to the extent that, because, how you're saying it, that you're concluding that this telephone was actually used by Mr. Tarculovski. Apart from that, I think we must say that we're talking about connection data and that it could be a further confirmation that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was actually using that phone, because the profile, in terms of usage, is not unusual because Mr. -- that it might be normal that -- that he is in connection with his colleagues, because he is also body-guard and he might have connections with them for whatever reasons. But you must also apply the same guidelines as we would apply them to us, and the level of identification that you're describing here certainly needs to be checked. I would also like to point out the third or fourth paragraph in the accompanying letter to the RFA number 92 where it is stated explicitly that the transmitted data cannot be assigned to the various users with utmost certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I have finished my statement. I'm just trying to gather my thoughts. So in the letter 92, there is the personal -- there is the list of the personnel in the security sector stated where all these names are listed, and as a second attachment, there is also so-called telephone list where, for example, under number 34 there is Milan [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keuhnel, before you go any further, can I ask you to close down your notes, please.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just made those notes during the conversation just now, and I've been trying to gather my thoughts. I don't know whether it's going to be necessary. I would like to carry on, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we've heard enough, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that for the period -- and again I'm talking of those telephone records for the period 10 to 12 of August of 2001, there is no recorded calls from this particular phone which you say was used by Mr. Tarculovski and any of the phones which you believed were used by Mr. Boskoski during that period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to reply to that question, I must also state that apart from these two telephone lists, of course we were submitted the other telephone lists, that we applied very strict guidelines, even to ourselves, and could not find -- establish an identification level that was 100 percent. As to the possible telephone numbers which were called by -- which were used by Mr. Ljube Boskoski or by his body-guards, the same principle applies again. With RFAs I think, I have to think about it, we were given about six mobile numbers, which owing to the RFA information were used by Ljube Boskoski during that time. Apart from that, we received parts of three land line numbers as well. So all in all, you could say that owing to the information that we received and also the interviews that we conducted with other body-guards, we could not establish an identification level which would have been 100 percent certain. The next possible step, of course, would have been to get a witness evidence, witness statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But let's just stay with the question, please, Mr. Kuehnel, if I may. Is it correct that you were not able, as you just indicated, to ascertain with any agree of certainty that any of the numbers that were given to you by the authorities as the telephone numbers used by Mr. Boskoski were in contact with the particular telephone which -- the record of which we have in front of us during the period 10 to 12 of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you want to summarize it like that, yes, you could say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that Mr. Keskovski, Zlatko, the head of the security of the president at the time, indicated and explained to you that it was he in fact who called Mr. Boskoski, on behalf of the president, in relation to the events of Ljuboten. Do you recall him saying that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness and counsel to pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, we are being asked to slow down between questions and answers. Mr. Kuehnel, I'd like to ask you something quite different now and it relates to the efforts which you and your colleague made to investigate the status of Mr. Atulla Qaili. And first perhaps as an introduction matter, is it correct that Mr. Qaili is listed as one of the alleged victims of a murder at Ljuboten? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] He is listed as being arrested and he -- consequently he died afterwards, so he is listed as a victim, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that you have come to the view that -- and again as far as the material that was available to you during your investigation, that there was no information available to you that would suggest that prior to his detention, as you called it, Mr. Qaili had been armed. Is that correct, is it the view you took?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply so that we understand your evidence fully, you're not saying that Mr. Qaili was not armed but your evidence is that insofar as the evidence that was able to you, you could not determine that this was the case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reply refers to him while being under arrest or during his time in detention, before that, that he had not had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Perhaps my question was not very clear, Mr. Kuehnel. Is it correct that your evidence as far as concerned whether or not Mr. Qaili had been armed prior to his detention, as you call it, is that you had no information, that he, in fact had been armed. You are not saying that he wasn't, but simply that you have or you had no information which would suggest that he had been armed prior to detention. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is -- the wording of the question is a bit difficult, but in principle, I can agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that there be would -- depending on the circumstances, there could be all sorts of indication that could be relevant to determining whether a person has or hasn't taken part in hostilities. Do you recall with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you could rephrase the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. As an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor, you are sometimes requested or expected to determine whether a particular individual took an active part in the hostilities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And to make that determination whether the person was in fact involved in the hostilities or not, you would rely on different factors and different elements. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the factors or elements which could be relevant to this determination would be the fact of whether or not the person in question had been, as you called it in your statement, armed or that is whether he carried or used weapons at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And I would like to say that whatever I said in my statement was applied to the moment of the arrest, at that moment when he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just going on with this question, you would agree with the general proposition that although the presence of nitrate and nitrite particles on someone's hands may have different explanations or different reasons, one of them is at least consistent with the fact that the person who had such particles on him or herself was carrying or using a gun. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the given conditions in Ljuboten and under the given state of knowledge that I have as a police officer and the information that I received from experts and also after reviewing the Macedonian files, I can say that there is a theoretical possibility but which is quite restricted here for the given reasons, but I don't want to go further into this discussion because I do not have the necessary expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. Do you recall perhaps following the evidence of Dr. Eichner in this courtroom that he also indicated that a possible explanation for the presence of nitrate particles on someone's hand would be the use or handling of a hand-grenade? Do you recall the evidence of Dr. Eichner on that point?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, basically, yes. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall the evidence perhaps of Mr. Jakovski as well, among others, to the effect that Mr. Qaili had tested positive to nitrate particles. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this was at least consistent or with the suggestion that Mr. Qaili could have been using a gun or carrying a gun or using or handling a hand-grenade at the time of what you say was his detention. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just wonder if perhaps that question -- it's a bit broad and a little vague because it refers to Mr. Qaili's detention and that there's a -- there's a gap in the time-period from the moment that he was initially detained until the very end when he was transferred to the hospital. And perhaps Mr. Mettraux can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you agree that the fact that Mr. Qaili tested positive to nitrate particles is consistent, first, with the possibility that he had used a weapon or that he had been carrying a weapon shortly prior to being tested. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one among other -- a lot of possibilities as to why such a test could come -- could have a positive result. There are several possibilities, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of these other possibilities would be the fact that Mr. Qaili had been handling a hand-grenade shortly before being tested. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a very theoretical discussion at the moment. It's a theoretical discussion about probability and likelihood. As I have already stated, it's one among several possibilities, contamination, other reasons. Contamination after the arrest, during transport. But, of course, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So when you say in your statement that had you no information in your possession suggested that Mr. Qaili had been armed at the time, in fact you took the view that this evidence was not conclusive and took the view that there must have been a, quote/unquote, innocent explanation for the presence of nitrate particles on Mr. Qaili's hands. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said before, this position referred to the moment of detention. I didn't mean by that or excluding the possibility to the extent that before or after detention the person in question had come into contact with the traces, either by touching it himself or by other contamination by some other means. As I say, this refers to the situation during the time of arrest by the police, and there are many statements from the people who were present when he was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, however, or are you aware of the fact that the local authorities took a different view of the matter and that in their view, the nitrate particle that were present on Mr. Qaili's hands at the time were consistent with criminal or, as they put it, terrorist activities. Is that correct? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Qaili Atulla was listed in one of the security lists as being allegedly in possession of a fire-arm. There was several people involved, and one of them was Mr. Qaili Atulla had who been associated with a particular fire-arm. So this is a possibility, in theory, of being contaminated by gunpowder. And -- but it's a possibility that you can see from the files that contamination with a gunpowder is suggested as being the result of contact with hand-grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that you had other information in your possession that suggested, at the least, that Mr. Qaili had in fact taken part in the hostilities, including by handling weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D1098, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, this is a document that comes from the UBK or DBK, as it is sometimes called, and it's a translation of a document that we received from the Office of the Prosecutor. The document itself is dated the 8th of May of 2002, and if you look at the subject matter it says that it refers to a conversation with the operative source Kmet, which was held on 16 April of 2002 between 1800 and 2000 hours. Do you recall seeing that document, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that this was one of the documents that I saw in the files of the -- from the DBK. Correct me if I'm wrong, but it should have been February of this year, that is, a year later, that I wrote the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I ask you to focus first on the first paragraph of that document under the heading: Content. I will read it out to you. It says this: "During the interview and in relation to the events related to the actions of the members of the so-called, 'NLA' in the village of Ljuboten during the past year, that is, the events including the politicised and dramatised in the public 'Ljuboten case' the operative source Kmet stated that from the village of Ljuboten and within the composition of paramilitary 'NLA' 29 persons were involved as fighters out of which the majority has been active in the Kumanovo-Lipkovo region." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please, I'll ask you, Mr. Kuehnel, to locate the paragraph in the middle of the document which starts with the word: "During the further course of the conversation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read out to you. It says this: "During the further course of the conversation, the source stated interesting information with regards to the intervention of the Macedonian security forces in the village of Ljuboten in the month of August in the past year. Namely, he stated data which shows that this intervention had been subject to armed response by some individuals. Therefore, around 10 persons, among which Atulla Qaili, killed during the fights, Ahmeti Ahmet, Ahmeti Adem, unknown person, son of Muharem Ramadani, son of Aziz Bajrami, and others had been brought in front of the house of Cajani Abdullah. Prior to that, these persons had fired towards the police with carbine and automatic rifles which they later hid in and under the fridge-freezer, but when the members of the MOI of Republic of Macedonia had entered into his house, they had not conducted any search, only detained the persons. And they could not find the hidden weapons." And then if you go down further on the page towards the end, there's a third section called: Operative worker's remark. The person say "I consider the information presented by the operative source Kmet to be objective and accurate." I would simply ask you this: Did you have that information in your possession at the time when you formed the view that there was no information in your possession that Mr. Qaili had been armed prior to detention?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My own investigations did not come up with the same result regarding Cajani Abdullah. As I said before, I think this document comes from the lot that I received from the UBK/DBK and this would explain why I got this information later.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Kuehnel, that at least one witness who was interviewed by your colleagues of the Office of the Prosecutor suggested that he had heard that Atulla Qaili had been handling a hand-grenade prior to his being detained? Are you aware of that information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the moment. Perhaps could you remind me?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if it is within the scope of your knowledge or recollection, do you recall a particular witness suggesting that he heard a conversation on the radio which suggested that the person who Mr. Qaili Atulla, who later died, had been handling a hand-grenade. Is that within your recollection or memory?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be an investigator's note from Mr. Zoran Cvetanovski something to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were some notes to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Kuehnel. I'd like to now turn to a different topic. You have been shown yesterday and have commented upon a number of documents. If you recall, those were documents that related to the records that you obtained concerning the registers of the MOI. Do you recall being shown those documents?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful, on Friday. Thank you for connecting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the transcript, this is now Exhibit P521 and P522. They were under tab 7 and 8 of the Prosecution binder of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Focussing first on the first such document, Mr. Kuehnel, the one that was given to you by Ms. Arsovska, you've indicated that Ms. Arsovska conducted a search which led to the production of that document, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the document with the investigator's notes? Is that what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I will show you the document, Mr. Kuehnel, that will be easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we please see Exhibit P521, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that document, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall suggesting that the result -- or the document in question was obtained as a result of a search conducted by Ms. Arsovska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the second such document which we may see in a moment, you indicated that it was the result of a search conducted by Mr. Besim Ramicevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just as a general matter, were you present when either or both of those search were conducted?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present with Madam Arsovska, and I received it from Mr. Besim Ramicevic personally. Whether I was standing beside him or not, I cannot recall at the time. But I think I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who conducted the search, the result of which were given to you by Mr. Ramicevic?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my memory, it was Mr. Ramicevic. But it's two or three years ago, but I think it was Mr. Ramicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you've indicated that you were not present when he conducted that search. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not really what I said. I got it from his hands and I seem to remember that I was there. But I received this directly from Mr. Ramicevic. Whether I was actually standing beside him or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, as a general matter, Mr. Kuehnel, do you know what sort of facilities, or search facilities in particular, Mr. Ramicevic and Ms. Arsovska had been using to locate and identify these particular documents?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They talked about it as the Krim-1 crime register search. There is probably another one too. But this has to do with Krim-1 register. This is the information system of the Macedonian Ministry of the Interior with regard to criminal records.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps my question was not very clear. But do you know what facility they had at their disposal to produce the set of documents which we have now in front of us? Do you know what facilities they used to identify and obtain these documents?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm tempted to say computer, but I don't really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Desktop. This was something that Ms. Arsovska was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so it is your understand that both Ms. Arsovska and Mr. Ramicevic used a computer software facility to identify those documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, I believe, that there were two places from which you obtained those document; one at the SVR level from Ms. Arsovska and one at the ministry level from Mr. Ramicevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your search was limited to identifying possible criminal records. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: My search was limited to this chapter 34, which was explained to me as being war crimes. And in the Criminal Code I read this, chapter 34 describes the paragraphs of - one moment please - 413 to 422.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come to the subject matter in a moment, Mr. Kuehnel. But at this stage I was asking you more specifically about the type of material which the search generated. Is it correct that you've indicated the range of subject matter, chapter 34, but in terms of the documents which this search was capable of generating, do you agree that they relate to so-called criminal reports, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, these are criminal records. I don't know whether this has to do with the cases that have been concluded or judgments or simply evidence. I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So in fact you are not aware to say what sort of documents or the range of documents which are being or which are capable of being generated by such a search. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on what I've just said I cannot really tell you whether these are concluded cases or judgments. I can only say that these are records of police criminal investigation, which are in the computer information system and anyone can have access to this. And I can stick to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I can take one category of such document which would be criminal reports, are you aware of the fact that oftentimes criminal reports are being made at the OVR level? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the OVR level, generally what you would have is a book in which those records would be kept and made, and I mean the records of criminal reports. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that professionally the police officers or -- would be required to forward on the criminal reports in question up to the SVR. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't think of any official specification or guideline because I didn't have access to this. But as far as I understand, these reports or -- referred to criminal charges in this case, and the hierarchy would be that they had to be reported to the SVR or the MOI. Otherwise, there would be no point in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, however, that you did not conduct a similar search at the OVR level? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's actually not correct, because we were on the OVR level, and we looked at the books and the files. We didn't conduct an electronic investigation, but we went to OVR Cair and looked through the entire files, and in -- in the various departments where these records were established, we had access to these, too. This refers to war crimes, which I'm sure would not be dealt with at a lower level at a police station where the files remained -- would remain. For example, where Mr. Ramicevic is stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful, and my question was not precise enough, Mr. Kuehnel. The question was, and you answered it I believe, that you could not and did not conduct any electronic search of the records at the OVR level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you put the question that way, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated as well that the -- I'm asking, is it correct that the only records at the OVR level that you reviewed was the OVR Cair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the entirety of this term. We were at OVR Cair, and on the level of OVR Cair, we looked at all the records which also came from the police station Cair and Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Kuehnel, that those records which you search and the result of which we still have on our screen do not record all investigative steps as might have been taken by the MOI. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is certainly possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For example, you certainly have become aware that they do not record a request or recommendation for exhumation or autopsy. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a request or recommendation for exhumation would certainly not be listed in a criminal record, because this is an operative measure. It's not facts which would be listed in a criminal register.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply first in terms of time-frame, is it correct that the period covered by this search which you conducted of the record was for the year 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. You can see this under number 2 on each of the printouts here, registered for the year 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would be correct also in relation to the other documents which you received from Mr. Ramicevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Without checking the documents, I'm quite sure that, under number 2, the year 2001 would be entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in other words, you did not conduct or request a similar search for the year 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I limited the inquiry to the year 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also, Mr. Kuehnel, that this particular type of search is limited to "known perpetrators" or known persons that are the subject of a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think perhaps, but I'm not sure, it's referring to a person, not to a fact. On the other hand, one can also see that under number 6, for example, it's listed whether the perpetrator is known or not. So, from that point of view, I can't really give you a precise answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. But would you agree that in any case as far as those two search are concerned, the Ramicevic and the Arsovska, there was no particular record of an incident which related to an unidentified or an unknown person, as it's known? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, and it may be obvious, Mr. Kuehnel, that this particular search or this type of search only relates to information which has been recorded into a particular document or a report and has then been forwarded on. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say yes or no to this question. It is, of course, the case that from an original investigation, entry would have to be made into the database. What you see here --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'd like to finish my answer. But I stopped in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you wish to add something, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the moment because I think my answer would be imprecise and wouldn't lead us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have the second break and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Kuehnel. When we left off we were looking at this documents concerning the result of a search which Mr. Ramicevic and Ms. Arsovska conducted for you. Do you agree with the proposition that if a criminal report had been done orally rather than in writing, this particular report would not have appeared on your search. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can follow your theory. But I have learned that within the system of the Macedonian police, an oral record was made. But I have never -- I didn't know about this. I don't think it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that if also a police officer makes an oral report or provides oral information about the possible commission of a crime to, let's say, the investigative judge, this would, again, not appear on this particular document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you can compare the two. It's not comparing like with like. If, as you're saying, a police officer informs an investigating judge about a particular fact, then I don't think you're comparing things that can be compared. You should rather ask whether the police officer will also draw up a report, which then, again, would end up in a criminal charge and which would then mean that a registration is made in the system. So this is the theoretical discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come in a second to a very practical example, but as a general proposition, you would agree with the suggestions that unless the report in question or the information in question, whether provided to the prosecutor, investigative judge or otherwise, unless this information is put in writing, the search that you conducted would not be capable of generating any hits in relation to that particular document. Is that correct? Or information.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could say yes, but as I've already mentioned, I think you're comparing two things that cannot be compared.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask then specifically about a particular document, if I may. This would be Exhibit P535, please. Mr. Kuehnel, you will recognise this is a document shown to you earlier by my colleague. This is the phone records of a phone that was used by Mr. Ljube Krstevski at the relevant time. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could please turn to the third page of that document, and I should perhaps specify first or ask you, is it correct that this is the list of outgoing calls; that is, calls going from the telephone of Mr. Krstevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be, but doesn't have to be. I believe it to be, but I've only got one page. Well, perhaps I apologise to the registry and to you, Mr. Kuehnel. Could we go back to the first page, please. And this is the first page of the record, Mr. Kuehnel. Do you agree if you look at the top left-hand corner, this suggest that this is outgoing and follows the number of Mr. Krstevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 3 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask you, Mr. Kuehnel, to go towards the end of the page at the bottom. And if you can look at the fourth line from the bottom. There's a number, a call that is recorded at 5.02 on the 14th of August of 2001 to the investigative judge on duty. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. And of course it describes a link between these two telephone numbers, but doesn't tell you what was being said during the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. But do you agree, for instance, that this particular record of a conversation between Mr. Krstevski and the investigative judge on duty on the 14th of August of 2001 did not appear in any of the records which you obtained from the SVR and the MOI for the year 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in police work it's quite normal that conversations take place between police officers and investigative judges. And in no police station in the world you might deduce that a conversation between these two persons which would result into a registration of their conversation. So I do agree with you, in other words, there has been no registration.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could turn now to exhibit P536, please. Mr. Kuehnel, this is the other side of the coin, so to say. This is the list of incoming calls on the telephone number of Mr. Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd ask the registry to please turn to page 5 of that document. And if we can scroll down a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, could you see towards the end or a bit below the middle of that listing on the 14th of August of 2001 again, at 4.59 that there was a call from the investigative judge on duty this time to the phone of Mr. Krstevski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, although I think have you stated it in your previous answer, this particular record of what happened on that particular occasion was not recorded in a document which was then elicited or identified by your search at the SVR or the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have indicated in your evidence in chief and I think briefly when you answered a question of mine that you had limited your search or the search criteria which you used to generate particular document to chapter 34 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you look at it like that, it's correct. But I didn't look for documents but for records regarding criminal activities pertaining to chapter 34, war crimes. So I was looking for criminal acts and not for documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct that chapter 34 of the Criminal Code relates to war crimes, on the one hand, and also other international crimes or violations of international law. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it also correct that you did not undertake a similar search for, let's say, ordinary crimes such as murders or rapes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. For this particular area and for this particular database, everything was limited to chapter 34, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you knew that at the time no state of war had been declared in the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps you will recall the evidence of Ms. Vilma Ruskovska, who indicated that in the year 2001 crimes that were related to the crisis in the country were prosecuted not as war crimes but as regular domestic crimes. Do you recall her saying that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally cannot remember it literally, expressis verbis, but I rely on your quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I'll read it for you, Mr. Kuehnel, in fairness. This is the transcript of the 6th of June of 2007. This is page 1528 and also 1582. At 1528 the following question was put to Ms. Ruskovska: "Is that correct at the time in the Republic of Macedonia no state of war had been declared?" And the answer is: "It was not declared." And then further on she is being asked: "And judges in the court before you were acting were not even considering applying international humanitarian law to certain events. Would that be correct?" "Yes." And then at 1582, still on the 6th of June 2007 the question was: "You treated these events under the domestic law as general crimes, severe breaches or less severe breaches under domestic law and did you not think that the conduct of the police or army would be subject of the international humanitarian law?" And she said yes. Is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that the only cases that -- or case that were looked at through the lens of humanitarian law was or were the cases that the prosecutor of Macedonia offered to transfer to the Office of the Prosecutor? I'm talking of five different cases. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: To some extent, I can agree with you. Nevertheless, I believed that it was necessary to carry out this search in order to get a balanced investigative approach, and without -- or with this -- this fact that there was no war, there are registrations heading -- under this heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that -- or I'm putting it to you that you were aware that there was in fact a number of investigation that were going on in relation to crimes relating to the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, I already mentioned it in my direct, there is one result regarding Kumanovo. There is the second result, which can be -- which is split up into various cases in the region of Ohrid, if I remember correctly. But, again, here I stated that I have received information that this was a case of human trafficking of organised crime. So this chapter is actually being used by the Macedonian judiciary system and I think it was only fair also to look at this particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you also knew, didn't you, that there were dozens, perhaps even hundreds, in any case, dozens of other investigation or cases that related to events relevant to the crisis that were being looked at in accordance other parts of the Criminal Code of Macedonia and which were related to the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could well be the case. But the order that I had in this particular case was to find out whether there had been violations against the war crimes regulations and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But surely you are aware also that one of the investigation which was going on at the time was the investigation into the events of Ljuboten as well as four other investigation that related to the alleged perpetrators of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, you mention these cases that we were sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Were you aware -- I apologise, perhaps the question was not very clear. But before those cases were actually sent to you, Mr. Kuehnel, you are aware, aren't you, that those five cases had been under investigation by the local authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find it difficult to give a precise answer to that question, because my knowledge is superficial. But I do know that investigations had been carried out. With regard to Ljuboten, I can say that there had been investigations, with regard to the Albanians who had been arrested there, and also investigations being carried out about the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you knew -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also know that apart from the four Albanian cases that also investigations were carried out relating to those cases, but I don't have any specific knowledge about those. I haven't read up on them and I have never been involved in working on these cases, so I wouldn't be able to give any precise information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But perhaps as a general question, is it correct that none of those five cases which you knew were being investigated at the local level appeared on the document which resulted from the search conducted by Ms. Arsovska and Mr. Ramecevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's obvious when you read these printouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct also that as far as you know, the state prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia at the time Mr. Stavre Dzikov, in September of 2001 during the deferral of these five cases including - of 2002, I apologise - during the deferral of these five cases to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal made it clear that the investigation into those event had been ongoing at the domestic level. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Stavre Dzikov was involved and that there has been a great deal of exchange of information and opinions but it really goes beyond me and I would -- could only report on hearsay and very knowledge which is full of gaps. I got some -- I gained some knowledge from reading the judicial records and from our own correspondence. But as I've already stated, I only joined the OTP in October 2003. I have never been involved in the work on the other cases, and only in retrospect I gained some knowledge about this period in time and about these events. I don't think I can give you any more information on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the information that you obtained in retrospect, as you put it, did it include an investigator note prepared by your colleague Mr. Tucker, in which he recorded the fact that the deputy primary public prosecutor Mr. Cakic had stated that the investigation into Ljuboten had already been opened, and it's a note of the 28th of November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible that I have seen this document. I know that Mr. Tucker has written a number of memos. It is it quite possible that I might have read it. But I cannot remember the -- exactly how it was worded.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record it is Exhibit 1D197.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is a letter by your colleague and superior, Mr. Lopez-Terres, chief of investigations, dated 22nd of May of 2002 which suggests that those five cases were currently under investigation in Macedonia. Is it within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember -- I can remember seeing such a document, such a letter and also others by Mr. Lopez-Terres. I think that's also a point that I have already mentioned with regard to the judiciary records and the request for the ballistic investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is, simply for the record, Exhibit 1D201.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps as a general question, Mr. Kuehnel, perhaps you have answered it already, but are you aware that the reason or one of the reason invoked by the Office of the Prosecutor in September of 2002 for the deferral of the five cases, including the case of Ljuboten, to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal was the risk of colliding investigations between your investigation and the investigation conducted at the local level. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you any reply to that, really. It's a possible reason, but I really haven't got a complete overview over that time-period and about all the decisions that were taken and by whom; hence if I confirm or if I disagree, I could only give you a very incomplete account.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, I will refer to Exhibit P391. That's the Prosecutor request for deferral, 5 September 2002, as well as Exhibit 1D213, which is the transcript of the deferral hearing, and the actual decision by the Trial Chamber it is Exhibit 1D218.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you also aware of the fact, Mr. Kuehnel, that a relatively large number of persons benefitted from an amnesty for crimes allegedly committed or actually committed in the year 2001. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I have knowledge of this decision about amnesties by Boris ... [as interpreted]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that the issue of -- perhaps before I proceed, Mr. Kuehnel, I believe you had mentioned the name Boris Trajkovski at page 75, line 16. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knowledge, this decision has been signed by the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Are you aware of the fact that the issue of the amnesty had been raised already prior and also during the negotiation of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again, I can say that I only have rudimentary knowledge of this, but I don't have a reliable comprehensive knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But are you perhaps aware of the fact that on the day of the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement the president of the Republic Boris Trajkovski sent a very public letter to the Secretary-General of NATO, Mr. Robertson, in which he made it clear that former members of the NLA would benefit from that amnesty. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible it may well be. But I can't really recall the document and its contents but it is certainly possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Exhibit 1D193.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, also that in the course of the year, towards the end of the year of 2001 the president actually granted a number of pardons to people who had been arrested in relation to crimes allegedly committed in the course and in relation to the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think this is the whole concept of amnesty, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And may I take it -- may I take your answer as a yes, you are aware that this took place?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think one could say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that a number of villagers from Ljuboten who had been taken and detained during the operation on the 12th of August benefitted from presidential pardons of that sort? In particular in the month of December of 2001.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that the Law on Amnesty applied not only to people who had already been charged and convicted of any crime related to the crisis but that it would also exempt from prosecution any person for whom there is reasonable doubt that he or she prepared or committed a criminal act related to the conflict. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not to that extent. I don't think that I have the necessary expertise to draw these conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can show you Exhibit P83. Mr. Kuehnel, this is the decree for the proclamation of the Law of Amnesty, and as you indicated it was signed by the president after having been adopted by the parliament and I would like to draw your attention to Article 1 of that law. And if the registry could enlarge it somewhat, please. And I would just like to read to you first the beginning of Article 1. It says this: "The law exempts from prosecutor -- from prosecution, discontinues the criminal proceedings, and fully exempts from execution of the sentence to imprisonment, hereinafter amnesty, citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, person with lawful residence, as well as person that have property or family in the Republic of Macedonia for whom there is reasonable doubt that they have prepared or committed criminal acts related to the conflict in the year 2001, conclusive [sic] of 26th September of 2001." Do you agree, Mr. Kuehnel, on the basis of that Article that the Law on Amnesty applied to three different categories of individuals: Those that had been convicted of an offence, those who were being prosecuted or charged with an offence, and those for whom there was reasonable doubt that they had committed such an offence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I can read the text. I do understand the sense of the syntax of the paragraph and I do agree. As far as the further implications of this paragraph, this is something I certainly cannot comment on, because I don't have the necessary expertise. I think that is a fair answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that to the extent that the authorities had been interested in prosecuting any case pursuant to chapter 34 of the Criminal Code, those acts would have been covered by the amnesty with the reservation which is on the next page of those cases that were being investigated by the Prosecution of this Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for me, this is a theoretical discussion. I really can't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree, Mr. Kuehnel, that this would explain that the only two incidents recorded in your search or as a result of your search and which related to chapter 34 of the Criminal Code were not in any way related to the crisis or the conflict, as you name it, but that they in fact were organised crime type of activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think you should reverse the origin and deduce anything from the daily application of this law. Basically these are war crimes in chapter 34, which, apparently, also were used in everyday judicial proceedings to deal with offences such as human trafficking and prostitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that in fact chapter 34 is not limited, as you suggest, to war crimes but includes war crimes and other violations of international law. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I think both of us have read the Article, but the title is war crimes. And of course I would readily admit that articles are included which may have a wider scope than this term in the heading. It's a question of how the paragraphs are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Exhibit P81, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 139 of the document. That would be N000-5405-139, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that the title of that chapter of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia, that's chapter 34, in fact refers to crimes against humanity and international law. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the first provision in that section, article 403 relates to genocide. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the next provision talks of war crimes against the civilian population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, supposedly. I don't really see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the document could be scrolled down a little bit so that Mr. Kuehnel could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see that Article 404 relates to war crimes again the civilian population.?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see part of the title, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. You can see the rest of Article 404 and then Article 405 relates to war crimes against wounded and ill. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. Do you agree that Article 406 relates to war crimes against prisoners of war, 407 to the use of unallowed combat means, 408 to organizing a group and instigation to genocide and war crime, and 409 to unlawfully killing and wounding of an enemy. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that Article 410 relates to unlawful confiscation of objects from killed and wounded on the battle ground, 411 to a violation of a parliamentarian, 412 to cruel behaviour with wounded, ill or with prisoner of war. 413 relates to unjustified delay in repatriation of prisoners of war, 414 to the destruction of cultural and historical monuments. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that Article 415 relate to instigation to aggressive war, 416 to abuse of international signs, 417 to racial or other discrimination, 418 to founding a slave relationship and transportation of persons in slavery. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux, I do agree, and 418 is the article concerning human trafficking.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that 419 relates to international terrorism, 420 to endangering persons under international protection, 421 taking hostages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. Do you agree that the last article of that section, Article 422 relates to the crime of piracy, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that in fact this section chapter 34 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia is in fact much broader and covers both acts that are regarded as war crimes but also all sorts of other violations of international law or, as the title suggests, crime against humanity. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree, and I haven't contested that so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now to continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15. Could the Chamber say that it would hope that in the course of tomorrow to find a convenient time when we can look at the completion of the present case for the Prosecution as a matter of timetable, and look ahead to timetabling the procedures that will follow that, with a view to allowing everybody to plan with a little more certainty how matters might progress. We suggest tomorrow, even though it could come in the course of Mr. Kuehnel's evidence, because it would seem we're reaching a point where it could be a profitable discussion and will make many matters of uncertainty clear for future planning. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of November, 2001, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
